name: GOV.UK Service Manual
tagline: Helping teams create and run great digital services that meet the Service Standard
project_type: government digital standards framework and guidance resource
sdg_alignment: SDG 16 - Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
dependency_risks: machinery of government reorganisations (GDS moved to DSIT 2024)

news_articles.headline: Introducing the next stage of the Service Manual

academic_citations: The Case of the UK's Government Digital Service: The Professionalisation of a Paradigmatic Public Digital Agency. Digital Government: Research and Practice. ACM. 2023.

policy_outcomes.description: GOV.UK consolidation of 1,700 government websites saved over £70 million per year in hosting costs
UK ranked 3rd in OECD 2023 digital government index; GOV.UK cited as an exemplar; Service Manual standards credited as foundational
Service Standard applied to all large government digital services from April 2014, structuring assessment and delivery of hundreds of public services

outcome_methodology: government audits, OECD benchmarking, service assessment pass/fail records
documented_limitations: applies primarily to UK central government; adoption in local government is advisory only
47% of central government services still lack a digital pathway as of 2025
governance_model: government-owned; maintained by Central Digital and Data Office (CDDO) and GDS within DSIT
curation_criteria: Content reflects the 14-point Service Standard; updated via community consultation and GDS editorial process
contributor_governance: GDS/CDDO editorial team with community-of-practice input; public GitHub repository accepts contributions
controversies: Ongoing debate about mandatory vs advisory application to devolved/local government
GDS influence perceived to have declined post-2016 following senior leadership departures

government_partnerships.name: Central Digital and Data Office (CDDO)
government_partnerships.role: primary owner of Service Standard from 2021

government_partnerships.name: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT)
